title: The condensed pages of the Typst commands
description: calc/i18n/command-pages.json, schema 1.0 (spec 2026-10-24-onglet-commandes-pages, REQ-001, D-10, D-15) -- what Woodcore's commands tab and the website show of each public command, written by hand in French, German and English: its one-sentence lead, three or four key points, and for each argument of its /// block its group, its status, its own sentence, two or three examples and, for an argument taking a fixed list of values, every value with what it does and the Typst call that shows it (compiled once by calc/tools/build_examples.py into examples/out/values/). The signature, the order of the arguments, their defaults and their types are NOT here: they are read from the signature and the /// block of lib/ (REQ-003), and calc/tools/command_pages.py refuses a disagreement between the two. Read by calc/tools/command_pages.py alone, which validates it against this schema and then checks what the walker cannot say: every text carries the three languages, a value's `text` names a set of `value-texts` that has it, a group is one of command_pages.GROUPS.

value-texts.description: Sets of what a value does, shared by the arguments that take the same values (display, style, role, the three positions, scope): by set, by the value as Typst reads it without its quotes, the sentence in three languages. A value names its set by its `text` being the set's name.

commands.description: By public command (build_reference.CATEGORIES), its page. A command without an entry has none: the tests refuse it (REQ-004, REQ-013).

lead.description: One sentence: what the command does. The tree shows it under the name and the search reads it (REQ-011).

keys.description: «L'essentiel»: three or four cards, a bold title and two lines (UI-004).

line.description: The line of the command where it is not a call -- a state, used as `#report-level.update(2)` -- written as it is used. Absent for a function: the line is composed from its arguments.

note.description: One line under the arguments: what is not an argument and still decides what is printed (#unit's defaults).

named.description: The arguments that are only another way to write one of the line's (name-calc:, value:, norm-ref:, ..rest), said in one sentence instead of a row each (UI-005).

arguments.description: By argument, as its /// bullet names it, in the order the page lists them inside each group.

positional.description: Written in the line without its name -- `#var(key, symbol, value, unit)` --, though the signature may also take it by name.

via.description: The sink of the signature this argument is read from (`..defaults` of #calc-defaults), where the signature does not declare it.

default.description: Its default, for an argument read from a sink alone (`via`): the signature cannot say it.

text.description: Its own sentence: what it does.

code.description: The code shown: a string, or {fr, de, en} where it holds words.

context.description: What a whole call assumes above it -- a variable it prints again --: compiled with it by tests/test_command_pages.py, not shown.

unrendered.description: Why the values of this argument have no print (their calls are not given): what each of them prints is a page of its own, #show-annexes'.

values.description: Every value the argument takes, as Typst writes it (a fine value between quotes, `none` too), with what it does and the call that shows it: the call's text in three languages where it holds words.
